concept.name: Volume-weighted moving average
concept.definition: A moving average in which each price is weighted by its bar's volume - bars traded on heavy volume pull the average toward them, so the line tracks where business was actually done rather than treating all bars equally.
concept.intuition: An SMA answers 'average price of the last n bars'; a VWMA answers 'average price weighted by how much traded in each of those bars.'
concept.mechanics: Multiply each close by its volume, sum over n periods, and divide by the sum of volume over n periods. Often compared against an equal-length SMA to judge whether volume-backed prices lead or lag the plain average.
concept.formula: VWMA(n) = sum(C_{t-i} x V_{t-i}, i=0..n-1) / sum(V_{t-i}, i=0..n-1).
concept.failure_modes: A single extreme-volume bar dominates the window, so the average jumps when it enters and again when it leaves; meaningless on instruments without reliable volume such as spot forex.
concept.misconceptions: VWMA is not VWAP: VWAP is cumulative from a session anchor, VWMA is a rolling n-period window - they answer different questions.
concept.example: Tulip Indicators' worked example: closes 81.59-83.61 with volumes around 3.8-7.7M give a first 5-period VWMA of 82.33, versus an equal-weighted SMA of 82.63.

citations.source: Volume Weighted Moving Average - Tulip Indicators
